designChallenge: The ordinary domain, chosen deliberately as the opposite of caliber-movement. Everybody already knows what leggings look like, so nothing can hide behind an unfamiliar object: a reader can tell instantly whether the imagery is right, whether the garment shown is the one being described, and whether the page feels like a place or like six stacked bands. Material is abundant here rather than scarce — garment photography, fabric texture, and movement footage are all easy to reach, and the free video libraries are strongest on exactly this subject — so a page that comes back thin cannot blame the archive. What to read off it: does the route flow, with sections that hand off to each other and something that carries across, or does it resolve into independent reveal-on-scroll blocks; do the size chart and the fabric specification find a form other than a table; and is the sourced imagery treated into one world or shipped as a set of unrelated rectangles. Convergence is the standing risk in this category, because generic activewear stock is the easiest thing on the internet to find and the least worth shipping.
prompt: This is the product page for the Contour legging, the one garment made by Halfmoon, a small activewear label. It is bought by people who have been disappointed by leggings before — sheer fabric, a waistband that rolls, a size chart that lied — and who will read carefully before buying. Redesign the site so it does justice to the garment.
promptContentOnly: This is the product page for the Contour legging, the one garment made by Halfmoon, a small activewear label. It is bought by people who have been disappointed by leggings before — sheer fabric, a waistband that rolls, a size chart that lied — and who will read carefully before buying. Design and build that page.
preserve: All six colourways with their exact names, prices, and per-colourway stock state, including the two that are sold out and cannot be added to the bag
The full size chart — every size row with its waist, hip, and inseam measurements in centimetres
The three inseam lengths and which sizes each is offered in
The fit finder, which takes a height and a usual size and returns a recommendation, including its unsure state
Every fabric fact: the composition, the weight, the opacity test result, the four-way stretch claim, and the gusset construction
All three customer reviews with their names, their stated height and size, and their fit notes
The returns statement — 60 days, free return shipping, and that worn-and-washed returns are accepted
The add-to-bag flow and the bag summary, which must name the chosen colourway, size, inseam, and price
